cohort: A population-based cohort of nearly 900,000 mothers in Norway who gave birth to their first singleton infant (at least 22 gestational weeks) between 1967 and 2007.
finding: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (preterm delivery, SGA, preeclampsia, cesarean section) are associated with an increased risk of having only one lifetime pregnancy, but this risk is significantly reduced if the child experiences perinatal loss.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with an increased relative risk of having only one lifetime pregnancy (1.24), which was significantly reduced to 0.67 if the child was lost during the perinatal period.
